title: Per-tenant audit profiles, RBAC assertion bridge, and KMS affinity lock
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: customers have requested finer-grained audit redaction and retention controls per tenant, while operators need a safe way to enforce RBAC v2 assertions and keep tenant KMS usage aligned with region pinning. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a per-tenant audit profile manifest that controls redaction profiles and retention tiers; 2) an RBAC assertion bridge which materializes conditional grants at runtime for operator-scoped actions; and 3) a small KMS affinity lock that pins the selected CMK family to a deployment region for tenancy-bound decrypt operations.

What this changes: Implements a tenant-facing audit_profiles.yaml schema (defaults + overrides), a runtime assertion bridge (pkg/auth/assertion_bridge) that evaluates RBAC v2 policy templates and emits short-lived operator assertions, and a KMS affinity shim (pkg/kms/affinity_lock) which prevents cross-region key usage when a tenant is region-locked. The changes are non-breaking by default: existing tenants inherit a safe default audit profile and KMS behavior remains unchanged unless a tenant profile opts-in.

Migration notes: The install/upgrade path adds a new configmap for audit profiles. For Hosted customers the control plane will inject a pre-filled tenant profile (with trace-level retained for 30d). For Dedicated/Private, operators should run upgrade script scripts/upgrade/2026-02-audit-profiles-migrate.sh to create per-tenant configmaps from legacy global audit settings.

Testing performed: Unit tests for assertion bridge policy rendering and TTL semantics; integration tests against a local KMS emulator asserting region-deny behavior; e2e smoke that exercises a tenant with a custom redaction profile and verifies anonymization pipeline. CI reported a flaky e2e-audit test which was rerun and passed.

Rollout plan: Canary deploy to staging -> enable for 2 pilot tenants with audit-level = "private" -> collect telemetry (audit-drop-rate, policy-evals/sec, kms-deny-count) -> ramp. Feature guarded behind operator flag enable_tenant_audit_profiles and opt-in per-tenant config.

Security review: SEC-209 approved with one follow-up (limit assertion TTL to 5m for operator grants). That change was implemented (assertion_bridge now enforces TTL clamp).

Rollback: disable enable_tenant_audit_profiles and delete any tenant-specific audit_profiles configmaps; KMS affinity is reverted to legacy behavior by disabling tenant_region_lock feature flag.

Checklist:
- [x] schema + CRD-like manifest for audit profiles
- [x] RBAC assertion bridge implementation + unit tests
- [x] KMS affinity enforcement shim + integration tests
- [x] migration script for operators
- [x] docs and release notes

Related: Linear ENG-5123 for implement plan, SEC-209 for security review, SUP-4321 related support ticket describing customer issue.

release_notes:
- Introduce per-tenant audit_profiles to control redaction and retention
- Add RBAC v2 assertion bridge to safely materialize operator-scoped grants with short TTL
- Enforce KMS region affinity for tenants that opt-in to region pinning
- Migration script provided for operators upgrading from global audit settings
